 JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
(hereinafter for brevity referred to as the 'Act') seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded and fixing contributory negligence upon him by the learned X Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes, MACT, Bengaluru (SCCH-16) (hereinafter for brevity referred to as the 'Tribunal')

entities.text: X Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes, MACT, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
, in its judgment and award dated 20.09.2019 passed in M.V.C.No.1684/2017.
2.

The summary of the case of the claimant before the Tribunal was that on the date of 12.12.2016 at about 8.10 a.m. while he was riding his motorcycle bearing registration No. TR-05-7048 along with pillion rider on Queen's Road, Bengaluru and reached near traffic Head Quarters Junction a Car bearing registration No.KA-01-MD- 2565 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came and dashed to the motorcycle of the claimant.
In the said road traffic accident he sustained severe injuries.
He was immediately taken to Hosmat Hospital where he was treated as inpatient.
Claimant stated that he was working as a Customer Support in Aditya Birla Minacs and was earning `15,000/- per month.
But due to accidental injuries he became permanently disabled and lost his earning capacity.
With this he has claimed a compensation of a sum of `15,00,000/- from respondent Nos.1 and 2, arraigning them as insurer and owner of the alleged offending motor Car respectively.
3. In response to the notice both the respondents appeared before the Tribunal and filed their statements of objections.

The first respondent though admitted issuance of Insurance Policy against alleged offending motor Car however, denied his liability the occurrence of road traffic accident in the manner as contended by the claimant in his claim petition and denied his liability to pay any compensation.
Respondent no.2 admitted the accident involving the vehicle but denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the motor Car.
He contended that the occurrence of the road traffic accident was solely due to the negligence of the claimant who was also the rider of the motorcycle.

sentences.text: Before the Tribunal, the claimant got himself examined as PW-1 and got marked 25 documents from Exs.P-1 to P-25.
He also examined one Dr. Krishan Prasad as PW-2.
Respondents have not adduced rebuttal evidence.
5. After analysing the evidence and the materials placed before it, the Tribunal awarded the compensation under the following heads with the sum shown as against them:

The Tribunal awarded compensation of a sum of `5,69,080/- and after deducting 50% towards contributory negligence on the part of the claimant, it awarded compensation of a sum of `2,84,540/- rounded off to `2,84,600/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation, holding Insurer liable to pay the said compensation and directed to deposit the award amount.
It is against the said judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the claimant has filed this appeal.
7. The respondent No.1 herein (insurer) is represented by its counsel.

Notice to respondent No.2 is dispensed with vide order dated 06.07.2022.
8.
Records from the Tribunal pertaining to the matter were called for and the same are placed before the Court.

sentences.text: Though this matter is listed for Admission, however, at the request of the learned counsels for the parties, the matter is taken up for its final disposal.
10. Heard the arguments of learned counsel from both side.
Perused the materials placed before this Court, including memorandum of appeal and impugned judgment.

11. Learned counsel for the appellant in his single sentence argument submitted that he would not press the appeal for enhancement of the compensation, however his only contention is that the Tribunal was at error in fixing 50% of the contributory negligence on the part of the claimant who was the rider of the motorcycle.
With this he submitted that the fastening of the contributory negligence on the part of the claimant be lifted.

Per contra, learned counsel for respondent no.1 Insurance Company in his argument submitted that it is after appreciating the manner of occurrence of accident, the Tribunal has rightly held that the claimant has contributed 50% towards negligence in the occurrence of road traffic accident, as such the impugned judgment does not warrant any interference at the hands of this Court.
12.

The evidence of PW-1 coupled with the scene of offence panchanama at Ex.P.5 and rough sketch at Ex.P.6 and the charge sheet at Ex.P.4 would go to show that the road traffic accident has occurred in a junction of four roads identified as Traffic Head Quarters junction.
The evidence of PW-1 coupled with these exhibits further go to show that the accident has occurred almost in the centre point of the junction where four roads have united.
It is not in dispute that the said traffic junction is one of the most busiest traffic junctions in the city of Bengaluru.
As such every rider or driver of the motor vehicles are required to be very cautious in riding or driving the motor vehicles in that area.
The claimant as PW-1 has stated that the driver of the motor Car bearing registration No.KA-01-MD-2565 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to him.

Admittedly,
no witness was examined from the respondent side.
As such, it is only the evidence of PW-1 coupled with the exhibits produced by him are required to be considered on the point.
13. The claimant as PW-1 in his evidence has stated that the accident has occurred at traffic head quarters junction when he reached the said place with his motorcycle.

Though he contended that, at that time, of all of a sudden the offending motor Car coming in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner dashed to him, however, in his cross-examination he has stated that on the said day there was huge traffic.
He specifically admitted that the accident has taken place at the central place of the junction.
His evidence also shows that the said traffic junction was provided with the traffic signal lights and they were functioning.
The witness has admitted as true that he stopped his motorcycle in the middle of the road on seeing the red signal.

This clearly go to show that by the time red signal lightened in the traffic light, he had already crossed his road and entered the centre point of the junction as such, as admitted by PW-1 and also as shown in the rough sketch of the panchanama at Ex.P.6 the point of the accident became is the centre point of the junction where the four roads have joined.

sentences.text: This clearly go to show that the rider of the motorcycle (claimant) ignoring the yellow light must have proceeded further as such by the time red light came he was already in the middle of the circle.

Similarly, the driver of the motor Car bearing registration No. KA-01- MD-2565 must also has shown hastiness that without waiting for the green light to glow, he must have run his motor Car immediately after seeing the yellow light which also made him to come to the very same centre point of - 10 - the junction, resulting in dashing of both the vehicle at the centre point of the junction.
14.

It is because as everybody knows that before flashing the red light in the traffic signal yellow light would come to caution the drivers and riders to stop their vehicles and before green light would come the yellow light will glow up to alert them to keep their vehicles ready to move after seeing the green light.
It is to the knowledge of everyone that only after the red light in the other roads' signals glow, the green light would flash or glow in that particular signal of the road which gives a clearance.

Thus, by the time green signal is given the other connecting roads' signals would generally have red signal, that too, particularly in the present case of accident the diagrammatic picture of which can be seen in Ex.P.6.

As such, if either of the parties i.e., the claimant as a rider of the motorcycle or the driver of the alleged offending Car had followed the traffic signal completely then the accident could have been avoided.
- 11 - Since both of them have shown their hastiness the road traffic accident had occurred.
As such, the finding of the Tribunal that there was contributory negligence on the part of the claimant as a rider of the motorcycle also cannot be found fault with.

However, considering the type of the vehicles where, the motorcycle of the claimant being a smaller vehicle compared to that of alleged offending motor Car, the percentage of contributory negligence that was fastened upon the claimant who was the rider of the motorcycle appears to be on the higher side.

That in the facts and circumstances of the case, the Tribunal should have fastened the contributory negligence on the part of the claimant who was the rider of the motorcycle at 25% instead of 50% and remaining 75% should have been fastened to the driver of the motor Car, who has been fastened with only 50%.
As such, for fixation of the contributory negligence at that particular percentage only the impugned judgment warrants interference of this Court.
The learned counsel for the appellant has specifically stated that he would not dispute the quantum of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal so also the learned counsel for respondent no.1.

Still after pursuing the evidence led in the matter and after perusing the exhibits marked from the claimant's side, I am of the view that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal under various heads in total amounting to `5,69,080/- does not warrant any modification.

As such,
by retaining the quantum of compensation as it is, it is only for the variation of percentage of Sri.Pulaknath vs The United India Ins. Co. Ltd on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55386017/
5 contributory negligence, the impugned judgment warrants interference.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part; while retaining the quantum of compensation awarded by the learned X Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes and MACT,
Bangalore - 13 -  (SCCH -16) dated 20.09.2019 in  M.V.C.No.1684/2017 the rate of  interest ordered, the fixation of  contributory negligence at 50% upon  the claimant by the Tribunal alone is  interfered with and the said contributory negligence is modified and reduced to 25%.

- 14 - (iii) The remaining portion of the impugned judgment and award regarding the release of the entire amount going to the share to the claimant remains unaltered.
Draw the modified award accordingly.
